doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: The late-1950s Basie band and closing
title: Wrap-up request and Joe Williams on the piano
summary: The interviewers try to wrap up, but Foster tells a story of Joe Williams failing to jump on a piano.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: On that note, I know you guys have to get up early, and I wish we could talk all night.
Oh, hell, let’s talk all night, let’s talk all night. You got us started here now.
We only scratched the surface of jazz, I mean—
You didn’t let us tell any Joe Williams stories.
Well let me hear the Joe Williams story.
We got to get a Joe Williams story.

Well there’s one Joe Williams story that comes to mind, where he was singing this torchy ballad, you know, and in the old days in the little cabarets, male vocalists, and female vocalists especially, some of them would like jump up on the piano to sing the ballad and take the mic with them and jump up on the piano and cross their ankles and sing, and everybody would just groove along with it. This one time, I don’t know where we were but Joe Williams tried to jump up on that piano and didn’t make it. And he tried again and again, and still didn’t make it. And so Frank Wess, Frank Wess has got a laugh that you can hear forever, you know, like on a clear day you can hear Frank Wess laugh
forever. And he started laughing and it was infectious, the whole band started, so Joe finally gave up and then stood up and sang the song like he should have in the first place.
And Joe will be watching that, that’s good. Anything else you want to add for us?
